sentences.zh: 列傳第五 ○石顯 桓赧弟散達 烏春溫敦蒲刺

translations.literal: Biographies 5 ○ Shi Xian, Huanhan's younger brother Sandá, Wuchun, Wendun Puci
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 5: Shi Xian; Huanhan and his younger brother Sandá; Wuchun; Wendun Puci

translations.literal: (Appended)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended biographies)

sentences.zh: 臘醅弟麻產 鈍恩 留可 阿疏 奚王回離保

translations.literal: Lapei's younger brother Machan, Dun'en, Liuke, A Shu, Xiwang Huilibao
translations.idiomatic: Lapei's younger brother Machan; Dun'en; Liuke; A Shu; Xiwang Huilibao

sentences.zh: 石顯，孩懶水烏林荅部人。

translations.literal: Shi Xian was a man of the Wulinzha tribe on the Hailan River.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xian was of the Wulinzha tribe on the Hailan River.

sentences.zh: 昭祖以條教約束諸部，石顯陸梁不可制。

translations.literal: Zhaozu used regulations and statutes to restrain the tribes, but Shi Xian was unruly and could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu sought to bind the tribes with law and custom, yet Shi Xian remained defiant and beyond control.

sentences.zh: 及昭祖沒于逼刺紀村，部人以柩歸，至孩懶水，石顯與完顏部窩忽窩出邀于路，攻而奪之柩，揚言曰：「汝輩以石魯為能而推尊之，吾今得之矣。」

translations.literal: When Zhaozu died at Biciji village and his tribesmen were bringing the coffin home, at the Hailan River Shi Xian and Wohuwochu of the Wanyan clan waylaid them on the road, attacked, and seized the coffin, proclaiming: "You honored Shilu for his ability—I have him now."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozu died at Biciji village and his people were escorting the coffin home, Shi Xian and Wohuwochu of the Wanyan clan ambushed them at the Hailan River, seized the bier by force, and cried out: "You made Shilu your leader for his prowess—I have him now."

sentences.zh: 昭祖之徒告于蒲馬太彎，與馬紀嶺劾保村完顏部蒙葛巴土等募軍追及之，與戰，複得柩。

translations.literal: Zhaozu's followers reported to Pumataiwan; together with Menggebatu of the Wanyan clan at Hebao village on Majiling and others they raised troops, overtook them, fought, and recovered the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu's followers appealed to Pumataiwan, who with Menggebatu of the Wanyan clan at Hebao village on Majiling and others mustered a force, overtook the raiders, fought them, and won the coffin back.

sentences.zh: 眾推景祖為諸部長，白山、耶悔、統門、耶懶、土骨論、五國皆從服。

translations.literal: The multitude acclaimed Jingzu as chief of the tribes; Baishan, Yehui, Tongmen, Yelang, Tugulun, and the Five States all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The clans then acclaimed Jingzu as head of the tribes, and Baishan, Yehui, Tongmen, Yelang, Tugulun, and the Five States all came under his authority.

sentences.zh: 及遼使曷魯林牙來索逋人，石顯皆拒阻不聽命，景祖攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: When Liao envoys led by Helu Linya came to demand fugitives, Shi Xian blocked them all and would not obey; Jingzu attacked him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao envoys under Helu Linya came to demand fugitives, Shi Xian barred their way and refused all orders. Jingzu attacked him but could not break his resistance.

sentences.zh: 景祖自度不可以力取，遂以詭計取之。

translations.literal: Jingzu judged that he could not take him by force and therefore used a stratagem to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu saw that force alone would not prevail and set about removing him by guile.

sentences.zh: 乃以石顯阻絕海東路請於遼，遼帝使人讓之曰：「汝何敢阻絕鷹路？

translations.literal: He reported to Liao that Shi Xian was obstructing the Eastern Sea route; the Liao emperor sent men to rebuke him, saying: "How dare you block the hawk road?
translations.idiomatic: He laid the matter before the Liao court, charging that Shi Xian was cutting off the Eastern Sea route. The Liao emperor sent envoys to rebuke him: "How dare you obstruct the hawk road?

sentences.zh: 審無他意，遣其酋長來。」

translations.literal: If you are found to harbor no other intent, send your tribal chief here."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean no treachery, send your tribal chief to court."

sentences.zh: 石顯使其長子婆諸刊入朝，曰：「不敢違大國之命。」

translations.literal: Shi Xian sent his eldest son Pojukan to court, saying: "I dare not defy the great state's command."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xian sent his eldest son Pojukan to the Liao court with the message: "I would not defy the great state's command."

sentences.zh: 遼人厚賜遣還，謂婆諸刊曰：「汝父信無他，宜身自入朝。」

translations.literal: The Liao richly rewarded him and sent him back, telling Pojukan: "Your father is truly without other designs; he ought to come to court in person."
translations.idiomatic: The Liao lavished gifts upon him and sent him home, saying to Pojukan: "Your father appears loyal; let him come to court himself."

sentences.zh: 石顯信之，明年入見於春搜，婆諸刊從。

translations.literal: Shi Xian believed this; the next year he appeared at the spring hunt, with Pojukan attending.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xian took them at their word. The following year he attended the spring hunt, Pojukan at his side.

sentences.zh: 遼主謂石顯曰：「罪惟在汝，不在汝子。」

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign said to Shi Xian: "Guilt rests on you alone, not on your son."
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor told Shi Xian: "The fault is yours alone, not your son's."

sentences.zh: 乃命婆諸刊還，而流石顯於邊地。

translations.literal: He then ordered Pojukan to return and banished Shi Xian to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pojukan back to his people and exiled Shi Xian to the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 蓋景祖以計除石顯而欲撫有其子與部人也。

translations.literal: This was because Jingzu had used a stratagem to remove Shi Xian while wishing to win over his son and tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jingzu had removed Shi Xian by stratagem while seeking to win over his son and his tribe.

sentences.zh: 婆諸刊蓄怨未發，會活刺渾水紇石烈部臘醅、麻產起兵，婆諸刊往從之。

translations.literal: Pojukan nursed resentment that had not yet broken forth; when Lapei and Machan of the Heshilie tribe on Huocihun River raised troops, Pojukan went to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Pojukan harbored a grudge not yet acted upon. When Lapei and Machan of the Heshilie tribe on the Huocihun River took up arms, he went to join them.

sentences.zh: 及敗于暮棱水，麻產先遁去，婆諸刊與臘醅就擒，及其黨與，皆獻之遼主。

translations.literal: When they were defeated at the Muleng River, Machan fled first; Pojukan and Lapei were captured, and with their partisans were all handed over to the Liao sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated at the Muleng River, Machan fled ahead of the rest. Pojukan and Lapei were taken, and they and their followers were all delivered to the Liao emperor.

sentences.zh: 久之，世祖複使人言曰：「婆諸刊不還，則其部人自知罪重，因此恐懼，不肯歸服。」

translations.literal: After a long while Shizu again sent men to say: "If Pojukan is not returned, his tribesmen will know their guilt is grave; in fear they will not submit."
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Shizu sent envoys again, saying: "Unless Pojukan is returned, his tribesmen will know their guilt is grave and, in their fear, will refuse to submit."

sentences.zh: 遼主以為然，遂遣婆諸刊及前後所獻罪人皆還之。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign thought this reasonable and therefore sent back Pojukan and all the culprits previously handed over.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor agreed and sent back Pojukan together with all the prisoners who had been surrendered before and since.

sentences.zh: 桓赧 弟散達

translations.literal: Huanhan, younger brother Sandá
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan and his younger brother Sandá

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達兄弟者，國相雅達之子也。

translations.literal: The brothers Huanhan and Sandá were sons of Yada, the state minister.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan and Sandá were sons of Yada, who held the office of state minister.

sentences.zh: 居完顏部邑屯村。

translations.literal: They dwelt at Yitun village in the Wanyan clan's territory.
translations.idiomatic: They lived at Yitun village in Wanyan territory.

sentences.zh: 雅達稱國相，不知其所從來。

translations.literal: Yada was called state minister; whence he came is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Yada bore the title of state minister, but his origins are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 景祖嘗以幣與馬求國相于雅達，雅達許之。

translations.literal: Jingzu once offered gifts and horses to request the state minister's office from Yada, and Yada agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu once sent gifts and horses to obtain the office of state minister from Yada, and Yada consented.

sentences.zh: 景祖得之，以命肅宗，其後撒改亦居是官焉。

translations.literal: Jingzu obtained it and appointed Suzong to it; afterward Sagai also held this office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu secured the post and gave it to Suzong; later Sagai would hold the same office.

sentences.zh: 桓赧兄弟嘗事景祖。

translations.literal: The Huanhan brothers had once served Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Huanhan had once served under Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，季父跋黑有異志，陰誘桓赧欲與為亂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's reign his uncle Bahei harbored divergent ambitions and secretly urged Huanhan to join him in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizu's reign his uncle Bahei nursed rebellious designs and secretly urged Huanhan to rise with him.

sentences.zh: 昭肅皇后往邑屯村，世祖、肅宗皆從行，遇桓赧、散達各被酒，言語紛爭，遂相毆擊，舉刃相向。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaosu went to Yitun village; Shizu and Suzong both accompanied her. They encountered Huanhan and Sandá, each drunk; words turned to quarrel, they came to blows, and blades were raised against one another.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaosu visited Yitun village with Shizu and Suzong in attendance. They met Huanhan and Sandá, both in their cups; argument led to blows, and blades were drawn.

sentences.zh: 昭肅皇后親解之，乃止，自是謀益甚。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaosu personally intervened and stopped them; from then on their plotting grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaosu herself parted them, and the affray ended—but from that day their conspiracy deepened.

sentences.zh: 是時烏春、窩謀罕亦與跋黑相結，詭以烏不屯賣甲為兵端，世祖不得已而與之和。

translations.literal: At this time Wuchun and Womouhan also joined with Bahei; on the pretext that Wubutun was selling armor they made it a cause for war, and Shizu, having no choice, made peace with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun and Womouhan had also thrown in with Bahei. They seized on Wubutun's sale of armor as a pretext for war, and Shizu, left no alternative, made peace with them.

sentences.zh: 間數年，烏春以其眾涉活論、來流二水，世祖親往拒之。

translations.literal: After several years Wuchun led his forces across the Huolun and Lailiu rivers; Shizu went in person to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later Wuchun marched his forces across the Huolun and Lailiu rivers, and Shizu went out in person to meet him.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達遂起兵。

translations.literal: Huanhan and Sandá thereupon raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan and Sandá then took up arms.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以偏師拒桓赧、散達。

translations.literal: Suzong with a detached force opposed Huanhan and Sandá.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong led a secondary force against Huanhan and Sandá.

sentences.zh: 世祖畏其合勢也，戒之曰：「可和則和，否則戰。」

translations.literal: Shizu feared they would combine their strength and warned him: "Make peace if you can; otherwise fight."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu feared a junction of enemy forces and instructed him: "Treat for peace if you can; otherwise give battle."

sentences.zh: 至斡魯紺出水，既陣成列，肅宗使盆德勃堇議和。

translations.literal: At the Wuluguan River, once the battle lines were formed, Suzong sent the tribal chief Pende to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: At the Wuluguan River, with the armies drawn up, Suzong sent the tribal chief Pende to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 桓赧亦恃烏春之在北也，無和意。

translations.literal: Huanhan also relied on Wuchun being in the north and had no mind for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan, counting on Wuchun's advance from the north, would not hear of peace.

sentences.zh: 盆德報肅宗曰：「敵欲戰。」

translations.literal: Pende reported to Suzong: "The enemy wishes to fight."
translations.idiomatic: Pende reported to Suzong: "The enemy is bent on battle."

sentences.zh: 或曰：「戰地迫近村墟，雖勝不能盡敵，宜退軍誘之寬地。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "The battlefield is close to villages; even if we win we cannot destroy the enemy entirely—we ought to withdraw and lure them to open ground."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged: "The field lies too near the settlements—even victory will not let us annihilate them. Withdraw and lure them onto open ground."

sentences.zh: 肅宗惑之，乃令軍少卻，未能成列。

translations.literal: Suzong was swayed and ordered the army to fall back slightly, but they could not keep their formation.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was persuaded and ordered a slight retreat, and the ranks broke apart.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達乘之，肅宗敗焉。

translations.literal: Huanhan and Sandá seized the moment; Suzong was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan and Sandá pressed the advantage, and Suzong was routed.

sentences.zh: 桓赧乘勝，大肆鈔略。

translations.literal: Huanhan followed up his victory and plundered on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan drove his victory home with widespread pillage.

sentences.zh: 是役也，烏春以久雨不能前，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: In this campaign Wuchun, because of prolonged rain, could not advance and therefore dismissed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In that same campaign Wuchun, halted by unending rain, broke off and withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞肅宗敗，乃自將，經舍很、貼割兩水取桓赧、散達之家、桓赧、散達不知也。

translations.literal: When Shizu heard that Suzong had been defeated he took command himself, passed by the Shehen and Tiege rivers, and struck at the homes of Huanhan and Sandá—they did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Suzong's defeat, Shizu took the field in person, marched by way of the Shehen and Tiege rivers, and fell upon the homes of Huanhan and Sandá before they knew what was happening.

sentences.zh: 世祖焚其所居，殺略百許人而還。

translations.literal: Shizu burned their dwellings, killed and plundered some hundred-odd persons, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He burned their settlements, killed and plundered a hundred or more, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 未至軍，肅宗之軍又敗。

translations.literal: Before he reached the army Suzong's force was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could rejoin the main force, Suzong's army was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 世祖至，責讓肅宗失利之狀，使歡都、冶訶以本部七謀克助之，複遣人議和。

translations.literal: When Shizu arrived he rebuked Suzong for his defeats, sent Huandu and Yehe with seven commanderies of their own tribe to assist him, and again sent men to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu came up, reproached Suzong for his losses, and sent Huandu and Yehe with seven commanderies of their tribe to reinforce him, while once more dispatching envoys to treat for peace.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達欲得盈歌之大赤馬、辭不失之紫騮馬，世祖不許，遂與不術魯部卜灰、蒲察部撒骨出及混同江左右匹古敦水北諸部兵皆會，厚集為陣，嗚鼓作氣馳騁。

translations.literal: Huanhan and Sandá demanded Yingge's great red horse and Cibushi's purple bay; Shizu refused. They then joined with Buhui of the Bushilu tribe, Saguchu of the Pucha tribe, and the forces of all tribes north of the Pigudun River on both banks of the Hun Tong River, massed thickly in battle array, beat drums, roused spirit, and charged.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan and Sandá demanded Yingge's great chestnut stallion and Cibushi's purple bay; Shizu refused. They then rallied Buhui of the Bushilu tribe, Saguchu of the Pucha tribe, and every clan north of the Pigudun on both sides of the Hun Tong, drew up a dense battle line, beat the drums, and charged with raised spears.

sentences.zh: 桓赧恃其眾，有必勝之心，下令曰：「今天門開矣，悉以爾車自隨。

translations.literal: Huanhan relied on his numbers and had a mind set on certain victory; he issued an order: "Heaven's gate is open today—bring all your carts with you.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his numbers, Huanhan was sure of victory and proclaimed: "Heaven's gate stands open—bring every cart you own.

sentences.zh: 凡烏古乃夫婦寶貨財產恣爾取之，有不從者俘略之而去。」

translations.literal: All the goods, treasures, and property of Wugunai's people—husbands and wives alike—you may take as you please; those who refuse, seize and carry off."
translations.idiomatic: Help yourselves to the goods and chattels of every Wugunai household; anyone who resists, take captive and be gone."

sentences.zh: 於是婆多吐水裴滿部斡不勃堇附于世祖，桓赧等縱火焚之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wobu, tribal chief of the Piman clan on the Botuoshui, attached himself to Shizu; Huanhan and the others set fire and burned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wobu, chief of the Piman clan on the Botuoshui, had sided with Shizu; Huanhan and his allies burned him alive.

sentences.zh: 斡不死，世祖厚撫其家，既定桓赧，以舊地還之。

translations.literal: Wobu did not die; Shizu richly comforted his household, and once Huanhan was settled, restored his former lands to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wobu survived. Shizu treated his family with great generosity and, once Huanhan was subdued, restored their former lands.

sentences.zh: 桓赧軍複來，蒲察部沙祗勃堇、胡補荅勃堇使阿喜間道來告，且問曰：「寇將至，吾屬何以待之？」

translations.literal: Huanhan's army came again; Shazhi, tribal chief of the Pucha tribe, and Hubuda, tribal chief, sent Axi by a hidden path to report and also to ask: "The enemy is about to arrive—how shall we deal with them?"
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan's army returned. Shazhi and Hubuda, tribal chiefs of the Pucha clan, sent Axi by a secret route to warn Shizu and to ask: "The enemy is near—what are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 世祖複命曰：「事至此，不及謀矣。

translations.literal: Shizu again ordered: "Matters have come to this—there is no time for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu replied: "Matters have gone too far for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 以眾從之，自救可也，惟以旗幟自別耳。」

translations.literal: Come with your forces and you may save yourselves—only distinguish yourselves by your banners."
translations.idiomatic: March with your full strength and you may yet save yourselves—only mark yourselves clearly by your banners."

sentences.zh: 每有兵至，則輒遣阿喜穿林潛來，令與畢察往還大道，即故潛往來林中路也。

translations.literal: Whenever troops approached he would send Axi through the forest by stealth; he was to travel the main road back and forth with Bicha—that is, the old secret route through the woods.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever enemy troops drew near, he sent Axi stealing through the forest—the same hidden woodland path by which he and Bicha had long passed messages along the main road.

sentences.zh: 桓赧至北隘甸，世祖將出兵，聞跋黑食于馳滿村死矣。

translations.literal: When Huanhan reached Beiaidian, Shizu was about to take the field when he heard that Bahei had died while dining at Chiman village.
translations.idiomatic: As Huanhan reached Beiaidian, Shizu was preparing to march when word came that Bahei had died at dinner in Chiman village.

sentences.zh: 乃沿安術虎水行，且欲並取海故術烈速勃堇之眾而後戰。

translations.literal: He then marched along the Anshuhu River, intending first to gather the forces of Haigu, the Sulie tribal chief, and then give battle.
translations.idiomatic: He marched along the Anshuhu River, planning first to win over the troops of Haigu, the Sulie tribal chief, before giving battle.

sentences.zh: 覘者來報曰：「敵至矣。」

translations.literal: Scouts came to report: "The enemy has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported: "The enemy is upon us."

sentences.zh: 世祖戒辭不失整軍速進，使待於脫豁改原。

translations.literal: Shizu warned Cibushi to keep his army in order and advance swiftly, and ordered him to wait at the Tuohuogai plain.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Cibushi to hold his ranks together and press forward at speed, and to await him on the Tuohuogai plain.

sentences.zh: 當是時，桓赧兵眾，世祖兵少，眾寡不敵。

translations.literal: At this time Huanhan's troops were many and Shizu's few—the odds were against him.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan's host far outnumbered Shizu's; the odds were hopeless.

sentences.zh: 比世祖至軍，士氣恤甚。

translations.literal: By the time Shizu reached the army, morale was deeply shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu reached the camp, the soldiers' spirits were utterly broken.

sentences.zh: 世祖心知之而不敢言，但令解甲少憩，以水洗面，飲鮮水。

translations.literal: Shizu knew it in his heart but dared not speak of it; he only ordered them to lay aside armor and rest briefly, to wash their faces with water, and to drink fresh water.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu saw it plainly but said nothing; he merely ordered the men to doff their armor, rest awhile, wash their faces, and drink fresh water.

sentences.zh: 頃之，士氣稍蘇息。

translations.literal: Before long morale revived somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long their spirits rallied a little.

sentences.zh: 是時，肅宗求救於遼，不在軍中。

translations.literal: At this time Suzong was seeking aid from Liao and was not in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was away seeking help from the Liao court and was not with the army.

sentences.zh: 將戰，世祖屏人獨與穆宗私語，兵敗，則就與肅宗乞師以報仇。

translations.literal: Before battle Shizu dismissed attendants and spoke privately with Muzong: if the army were defeated, he would go to Suzong and beg troops for revenge.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle Shizu sent everyone away and spoke privately with Muzong: if the day went against them, he would join Suzong and beg Liao troops for vengeance.

sentences.zh: 仍令穆宗勿預戰事，介馬以觀勝負，先圖去就。

translations.literal: He also ordered Muzong not to take part in the fighting but to saddle a spare horse and watch the outcome, planning his course of withdrawal in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He told Muzong to keep out of the fighting, mount a spare horse, watch how the battle turned, and be ready to flee.

sentences.zh: 乃袒袖韔弓服矢，以縕袍下幅護前後心，三揚旗，三撾鼓，棄旗提劍，身為軍鋒，盡銳搏戰。

translations.literal: Then he bared his arms, slung his bow case and wore his arrows, used the hem of his padded robe to guard chest and back, thrice raised the banner, thrice beat the drum, cast aside the banner and took up his sword, placed himself at the army's point, and fought with all his sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped to the arms, slung bow and quiver, bound the skirt of his padded coat across chest and back, thrice raised the standard and thrice struck the drum, then cast aside the banner, seized his sword, took the van himself, and threw every man into the fight.

sentences.zh: 桓赧步軍以幹盾進，世祖之眾以長槍擊之，步軍大敗。

translations.literal: Huanhan's infantry advanced with dry shields; Shizu's men struck them with long spears and the infantry was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhan's foot soldiers came forward behind wicker shields; Shizu's men drove them back with long spears and broke the infantry completely.

sentences.zh: 辭不失從後奮擊之，桓赧之騎兵亦敗。

translations.literal: Cibushi charged fiercely from the rear; Huanhan's cavalry was also defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Cibushi fell upon them from the rear with a furious charge, and Huanhan's horsemen were routed as well.

sentences.zh: 世祖乘勝逐北，破多退水水為之赤。

translations.literal: Shizu followed up his victory in pursuit; at the Poduotui River the water ran red.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu pressed the pursuit, and at the Poduotui River the waters ran red.

sentences.zh: 世祖止軍勿追，盡獲所棄車甲馬牛軍實，以戰勝告於天地，頒所獲於將士，各以功為差。

translations.literal: Shizu halted the army from further pursuit, recovered all the abandoned carts, armor, horses, cattle, and military stores, reported the victory to Heaven and Earth, and distributed the spoils among the officers and soldiers according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: He halted the pursuit, gathered every abandoned cart, weapon, horse, and store, offered thanks for victory to Heaven and Earth, and divided the spoils among his officers and men according to their deeds.

sentences.zh: 未幾，桓赧、散達俱以其屬來降。

translations.literal: Before long Huanhan and Sandá both came to submit with their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huanhan and Sandá arrived with their followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 卜灰猶保撒阿辣村，招之不出。

translations.literal: Buhui still held Saala village and could not be summoned out.
translations.idiomatic: Buhui still held Saala village and would not come out though summoned.

sentences.zh: 撒骨出據阿魯紺出村，世祖遣人與之議和，撒骨出謾言為戲，答之曰：「我本欲和，壯士巴的懣不肯和，泣而謂我曰：'若果與和，則美衣肥羊不可複得。

translations.literal: Saguchu held Aluchu village; Shizu sent men to negotiate peace with him. Saguchu spoke in mockery and jest, answering: "I myself wished for peace, but the warrior Bade's Man would not agree; weeping he told me: 'If we truly make peace, fine clothes and fat sheep cannot be had again.
translations.idiomatic: Saguchu held Aluchu village. Shizu sent envoys to treat for peace, but Saguchu answered in mockery: "I was ready to make peace, but the warrior Bade's Man refused. Weeping, he told me: 'If we truly sue for peace, there will be no more fine robes and fat sheep.

sentences.zh: '是以不敢從命。」

translations.literal: Therefore I dare not obey your command."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I dare not accept your terms."

sentences.zh: 遂縱兵俘略鄰近村墅。

translations.literal: He then unleashed his troops to seize and plunder neighboring villages and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: He then let his soldiers loose to raid the neighboring settlements.

sentences.zh: 有人從道傍射之，中口死。

translations.literal: Someone shot him from the roadside; the arrow struck his mouth and he died.
translations.idiomatic: A man shot him from the wayside; the arrow struck his mouth and killed him.

sentences.zh: 卜灰之屬曰石魯，石魯之母嫁丁馳滿部達魯罕勃堇而為之妾。

translations.literal: Among Buhui's followers was one called Shilu; Shilu's mother had married Daluhan, tribal chief of the Dingchiman tribe, and become his concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Among Buhui's followers was a man named Shilu, whose mother had married Daluhan, tribal chief of the Dingchiman clan, and become his concubine.

sentences.zh: 達魯罕與族兄弟抹腮引勃堇俱事世祖，世祖欲間石魯于卜灰，謂達魯罕曰：「汝之事我，不如抹腮引之堅固也。」

translations.literal: Daluhan and his clansman Mosaiyin, tribal chief, both served Shizu. Shizu wished to set Shilu against Buhui and said to Daluhan: "Your service to me is not as steadfast as Mosaiyin's."
translations.idiomatic: Daluhan and his kinsman Mosaiyin, a tribal chief, both served Shizu. Wishing to drive a wedge between Shilu and Buhui, Shizu told Daluhan: "Your loyalty to me is not so firm as Mosaiyin's."

sentences.zh: 蓋謂石魯母子一彼焉，一此焉，以此撼石魯。

translations.literal: This was because Shilu and his mother were divided—one on that side, one on this—and by this he sought to shake Shilu.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that mother and son stood on opposite sides, and by this he hoped to unsettle Shilu.

sentences.zh: 石魯聞之，遂殺卜灰而降。

translations.literal: When Shilu heard this he thereupon killed Buhui and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Shilu killed Buhui and came over to Shizu.

sentences.zh: 石魯通于卜灰之妾，常懼得罪，及聞世祖言，惑之，使告于達魯罕曰：「將殺卜灰而來，汝待我于江。」

translations.literal: Shilu had relations with Buhui's concubine and always feared exposure; when he heard Shizu's words he was unsettled and sent word to Daluhan: "I am about to kill Buhui and come to you—wait for me at the river."
translations.idiomatic: Shilu had been intimate with Buhui's concubine and lived in fear of discovery. Shizu's words unsettled him, and he sent word to Daluhan: "I mean to kill Buhui and come to you—wait for me at the river."

sentences.zh: 伺卜灰睡熟，剚刃於胸而殺之。

translations.literal: He waited until Buhui was fast asleep, then plunged a blade into his chest and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He waited until Buhui slept, then drove a blade into his chest and killed him.

sentences.zh: 追者急，白日露鼻匿水中，逮夜，至江，方遊以濟。

translations.literal: Pursuers were pressing; in broad daylight he exposed only his nose above the water to hide, and at night, reaching the river, swam across.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers pressed close; by day he hid in the water with only his nose above the surface, and at night reached the river and swam across.

sentences.zh: 達魯罕使人待之，乃得免。

translations.literal: Daluhan had sent men to wait for him, and so he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Daluhan had posted men to receive him, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 久之，醉酒，而與達魯罕狠爭，達魯罕殺之。

translations.literal: After a long while, drunk, he quarreled fiercely with Daluhan, and Daluhan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, in his cups, he quarreled bitterly with Daluhan, and Daluhan killed him.

sentences.zh: 烏春，阿跋斯水溫都部人，以鍛鐵為業。

translations.literal: Wuchun was a man of the Wendu tribe on the Abasi River and worked at forging iron.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun was of the Wendu tribe on the Abasi River and earned his living as a smith.

sentences.zh: 因歲歉，策杖負簷與其族屬來歸。

translations.literal: Because of a lean year he took staff and pack and came to submit with his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, he took staff and pack and came in with his clansmen to submit.

sentences.zh: 景祖與之處，以本業自給。

translations.literal: Jingzu kept him and let him support himself by his trade.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu took him in and let him live by his craft.

sentences.zh: 既而知其果敢善斷，命為本部長，仍遣族人盆德送歸舊部。

translations.literal: Once he knew him to be bold, resolute, and decisive, he appointed him tribal chief of his own division and sent his clansman Pende to escort him back to his former tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that he was bold and decisive, Jingzu made him chief of his own division and sent his clansman Pende to escort him home to his former tribe.

sentences.zh: 盆德，烏春之甥也。

translations.literal: Pende was Wuchun's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Pende was Wuchun's nephew.

sentences.zh: 世祖初嗣節度使，叔父跋黑陰懷覬覦，間誘桓赧、散達兄弟及烏春、窩謀罕等。

translations.literal: When Shizu first succeeded to the military commissionership, his uncle Bahei secretly harbored covetous designs and from time to time enticed the brothers Huanhan and Sandá, Wuchun, Womouhan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu first inherited the military commissionership, his uncle Bahei secretly coveted the post and worked to win over Huanhan, Sandá, Wuchun, Womouhan, and others.

sentences.zh: 烏春以跋黑居肘腋為變，信之，由是頗貳于世祖，而虐用其部人。

translations.literal: Wuchun, because Bahei was close at hand as a source of trouble, trusted him and from this became somewhat disloyal to Shizu, while tyrannizing over his tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun, with Bahei so near and ready to make trouble, put faith in him, grew disloyal toward Shizu, and began to tyrannize over his tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 部人訴于世祖，世祖使人讓之曰：「吾父信任汝，以汝為部長。

translations.literal: His tribesmen appealed to Shizu; Shizu sent men to rebuke him, saying: "My father trusted you and made you tribal chief.
translations.idiomatic: His tribesmen appealed to Shizu, who sent envoys to rebuke him: "My father trusted you and made you tribal chief.

sentences.zh: 今人告汝有實狀，殺無罪人，聽訟不平，自今不得複爾為也。」

translations.literal: Now people report you with substantiated charges—killing the guiltless, judging cases unfairly—from today you must not do such things again."
translations.idiomatic: Men now bring proven charges against you—killing the innocent and judging unfairly. You must not do such things again."

sentences.zh: 烏春曰：「吾與汝父等輩舊人，汝為長能幾日，于汝何事。

translations.literal: Wuchun said: "I am an old companion of your father's generation—how many days have you been chief? What business is it of yours?
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun replied: "I am an old companion of your father's generation. How long have you been chief? What is it to you?

sentences.zh: 世祖內畏跋黑，恐郡朋為變，故曲意懷撫，而欲以婚姻結其歡心。

translations.literal: Shizu inwardly feared Bahei and dreaded that the tribal chiefs would rise in revolt; therefore he treated Wuchun with indulgent kindness and wished to bind his goodwill through marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu feared Bahei within and dreaded a general rising among the tribal chiefs; he therefore treated Wuchun with studied kindness and sought to win him through a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 使與約婚，烏春不欲，笑曰：「狗彘之子同處，豈能生育。

translations.literal: He had them arrange a marriage alliance; Wuchun did not wish it and laughed, saying: "The offspring of dogs and swine dwelling together—how could they breed?
translations.idiomatic: Shizu proposed a marriage tie; Wuchun refused and laughed. "When the sons of dogs and swine share one roof," he said, "can they truly bear young?

sentences.zh: 胡裏改與女直豈可為親也。」

translations.literal: How could one of Huligai take a Jurchen for kin?"
translations.idiomatic: How could a man of Huligai become kin to Jurchens?"

sentences.zh: 烏春欲發兵，而世祖待之如初，無以為端。

translations.literal: Wuchun wished to raise troops, but Shizu treated him as before and gave no opening.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun meant to take up arms, yet Shizu continued to treat him as always and offered no pretext.

sentences.zh: 加古部烏不屯，亦鐵工也，以被甲九十來售。

translations.literal: Wubutun of the Jiagu tribe, also an ironsmith, came to sell ninety suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: Wubutun of the Jiagu clan, likewise a smith, brought ninety suits of armor to sell.

sentences.zh: 烏春聞之，使人來讓曰：「甲，吾甲也。

translations.literal: When Wuchun heard of it he sent men to rebuke him, saying: "The armor is my armor.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun heard of it and sent men to protest: "That armor is mine.

sentences.zh: 來流水以南、匹古敦水以北，皆吾土也。

translations.literal: South of the Lailiu River and north of the Pigudun River—all is my territory.
translations.idiomatic: Everything south of the Lailiu and north of the Pigudun is my land.

sentences.zh: 何故輒取吾甲，其亟以歸我。」

translations.literal: Why do you seize my armor without cause? Return it to me at once."
translations.idiomatic: Why do you seize my armor? Send it back at once."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「彼以甲來市，吾與直而售之。」

translations.literal: Shizu said: "He brought the armor to market; I paid fair price and bought it."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu replied: "He came to sell the armor. I paid a fair price and bought it lawfully."

sentences.zh: 烏春曰：「汝不肯與我甲而為和解，則使汝叔之子斜葛及廝勒來。」

translations.literal: Wuchun said: "If you will not give me the armor yet wish reconciliation, then send your uncle's son Xiege and Sile here."
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun said: "If you refuse the armor but still want peace, send your uncle's son Xiege and Sile."

sentences.zh: 斜葛蓋跋黑之子也。

translations.literal: Xiege was Bahei's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege was Bahei's son.

sentences.zh: 世祖度其意非真肯議和者，將以有為也，不欲遣。

translations.literal: Shizu judged that his intent was not truly to treat for peace and that he meant to make trouble; he did not wish to send them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu saw that Wuchun did not truly mean peace and intended mischief; he was reluctant to send them.

sentences.zh: 眾固請曰：「不遣則必用兵。」

translations.literal: The multitude pressed him, saying: "If you do not send them, he will surely use force."
translations.idiomatic: His men pressed him: "Refuse, and he will certainly make war."

sentences.zh: 不得已，遣之。

translations.literal: Having no alternative, he sent them.
translations.idiomatic: Left no choice, he sent them.

sentences.zh: 謂廝勒曰：「斜葛無害。

translations.literal: He told Sile: "Xiege will come to no harm.
translations.idiomatic: He told Sile: "Xiege will not be harmed.

sentences.zh: 彼且執汝矣，半途辭疾勿往。」

translations.literal: But they will seize you—plead illness halfway and do not go on."
translations.idiomatic: But they mean to seize you. Plead illness on the road and turn back."

sentences.zh: 既行，廝勒曰：「我疾作，將止不往。」

translations.literal: Once they set out, Sile said: "My illness has come on; I shall stop and not go."
translations.idiomatic: On the march Sile said: "My sickness has flared; I will go no farther."

sentences.zh: 斜葛曰：「吾亦不能獨往矣。」

translations.literal: Xiege said: "I too cannot go alone."
translations.idiomatic: Xiege said: "I cannot go on alone either."

sentences.zh: 同行者強之使行。

translations.literal: Their companions forced them to go on.
translations.idiomatic: Those with them forced the two to continue.

sentences.zh: 既見烏春，烏春與斜葛厚為禮，而果執廝勒，曰：得甲則生，否則殺汝。」

translations.literal: When they met Wuchun, Wuchun treated Xiege with great courtesy but indeed seized Sile, saying: Give back the armor and you live; refuse and you die."
translations.idiomatic: When they came before Wuchun, he showed Xiege every courtesy, then seized Sile and said: Return the armor and live; refuse and die."

sentences.zh: 世祖與其甲，廝勒乃得歸。

translations.literal: Shizu gave up the armor, and only then did Sile return.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu yielded the armor, and Sile was released.

sentences.zh: 烏春自此益無所憚。

translations.literal: From this Wuchun grew ever more without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: After this Wuchun grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 後數年，烏春舉兵來戰，道斜寸嶺，涉活論、來流水，舍於術虎部阿裏矮村滓布乃勃堇家。

translations.literal: Some years later Wuchun raised troops and came to fight, taking the Xiecun ridge, crossing the Huolun and Lailiu rivers, and lodging at the home of Zibunai, tribal chief of Ali'ai village in the Shuhu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Wuchun marched to war by the Xiecun ridge, crossed the Huolun and Lailiu rivers, and quartered at the house of Zibunai, chief of Ali'ai village in the Shuhu clan.

sentences.zh: 是時十月中，大雨累晝夜不止，冰澌覆地，烏春不能進，乃引去。

translations.literal: It was the tenth month; heavy rain fell day and night without cease, ice slush covered the ground, Wuchun could not advance, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: It was mid-autumn. Rain fell for days and nights without pause; ice slush glazed the ground. Wuchun could not advance and drew off.

sentences.zh: 於是桓赧、散達亦舉兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huanhan and Sandá also raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Then Huanhan and Sandá took up arms as well.

sentences.zh: 世祖自拒烏春，而使肅宗拒桓赧。

translations.literal: Shizu himself faced Wuchun and sent Suzong to face Huanhan.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu met Wuchun in person and sent Suzong against Huanhan.

sentences.zh: 巳而烏春遇雨歸，叔父跋黑亦死，故世祖得並力於桓赧、散達，一戰而遂敗之。

translations.literal: Before long Wuchun returned on account of the rain, and his uncle Bahei also died; thus Shizu could combine his forces against Huanhan and Sandá and in a single battle defeated them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wuchun turned back in the rain, and his uncle Bahei died as well. Shizu could then concentrate against Huanhan and Sandá and rout them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 斡勒部人杯乃，舊事景祖，至是亦有他志，徙于南畢懇忒村，遂以縱火誣歡都，欲因此除去之，語在《歡都傳》中。

translations.literal: Beinai of the Wole tribe had long served Jingzu; by now he too harbored other intentions, moved to South Bijikente village, and by setting fires framed Huandu, wishing thereby to remove him—the account is in the Huandu biography.
translations.idiomatic: Beinai of the Wole clan had once served Jingzu; he too now turned disloyal, settled at South Bijikente village, and tried to destroy Huandu by framing him for arson—the full account is in Huandu's biography.

sentences.zh: 世祖獲杯乃，釋其罪，杯乃終不自安，徙居吐窟村，與烏春、窩謀罕結約。

translations.literal: Shizu captured Beinai and released him from guilt, but Beinai never felt secure; he moved to Tuku village and made a pact with Wuchun and Womouhan.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu took Beinai prisoner, then pardoned him, but Beinai could not rest easy. He removed to Tuku village and allied with Wuchun and Womouhan.

sentences.zh: 烏春舉兵度嶺，世祖駐軍屋辟村以待之。

translations.literal: Wuchun raised troops and crossed the ridge; Shizu encamped at Wupi village to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun marched over the ridge with an army; Shizu waited at Wupi village.

sentences.zh: 進至蘇素海甸，兩軍皆陣，將戰，世祖不親戰，命肅宗以左軍戰，斜列、辭不失助之，征異夢也。

translations.literal: Advancing to the Susuhai moor, both armies drew up and were about to fight; Shizu did not fight in person but ordered Suzong to engage with the left wing, with Xielie and Cibushi to assist—this fulfilled an extraordinary dream.
translations.idiomatic: At the Susuhai moor both hosts formed for battle. Shizu did not fight in person but ordered Suzong to lead the left wing, with Xielie and Cibushi to support him—fulfilling a strange dream of conquest.

sentences.zh: 肅宗束縕縱火，大風從後起，火熾烈，時八月，野草尚青，火盡燎，煙焰張天。

translations.literal: Suzong bound straw and set fire; a great wind rose from behind, the blaze fierce; it was the eighth month and the wild grass was still green, yet the fire burned it all, smoke and flame filling the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong bound straw into torches and set them alight. A strong wind rose at his back; though it was still the green of August, the blaze ran through the grass until smoke and flame filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 烏春軍在下風，肅宗自上風擊之，烏春大敗，複獲杯乃，獻於遼，而城蘇素海甸以據之。

translations.literal: Wuchun's army was downwind; Suzong struck from upwind and Wuchun was utterly defeated. Beinai was captured again and handed over to Liao, and a fort was built at the Susuhai moor to hold the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun's host stood downwind. Suzong attacked from above; Wuchun was routed. Beinai was taken again and sent to the Liao court, and Shizu walled the Susuhai moor to hold it.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈臘醅、麻產與世祖戰于野鵲水。

translations.literal: Lapei and Machan of the Heshilie tribe fought Shizu at Yaque River.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei and Machan of the Heshilie clan met Shizu in battle at Yaque River.

sentences.zh: 世祖中四創，軍敗。

translations.literal: Shizu received four wounds and the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu took four wounds and his army was beaten.

sentences.zh: 臘醅使舊賊禿罕等過青嶺，見烏春，賂諸部與之交結。

translations.literal: Lapei sent his former outlaw Tuohan and others over Qingling to see Wuchun, bribing various tribes to join with him.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei sent the old bandit Tuohan and others across Qingling to Wuchun, buying alliances among the tribes.

sentences.zh: 臘醅、麻產求助於烏春，烏春以姑裏甸兵百十七人助之。

translations.literal: Lapei and Machan sought aid from Wuchun, and Wuchun sent one hundred seventeen soldiers from Guli district to help them.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei and Machan sought Wuchun's aid; he sent one hundred seventeen men from Guli district.

sentences.zh: 世祖擒臘醅獻於遼主，並言烏春助兵之狀，仍以不修鷹道罪之。

translations.literal: Shizu captured Lapei and presented him to the Liao sovereign, also reporting how Wuchun had aided him with troops, and further charged him with neglect of the hawk road.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu seized Lapei and sent him to the Liao emperor, reporting Wuchun's aid as well and charging Wuchun with failing to maintain the hawk tribute road.

sentences.zh: 遼主使人至烏春問狀，烏春懼，乃為讕言以告曰：「未嘗與臘醅為助也。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign sent men to Wuchun to inquire; Wuchun was afraid and spun deceitful words, saying: "I never aided Lapei.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor sent envoys to question Wuchun. In fear he lied: "I never aided Lapei.

sentences.zh: 德鄰石之北，姑裏甸之民，所管不及此。」

translations.literal: North of Delin stone, the people of Guli district—what I administer does not reach here."
translations.idiomatic: North of Delin stone—the folk of Guli are beyond what I rule."

sentences.zh: 臘醅既敗，世祖盡得烏春姑裏甸助兵一百十七人，而使其卒長斡善、斡脫往招其眾，繼遣斜缽勃堇撫定之。

translations.literal: After Lapei's defeat Shizu took all one hundred seventeen of Wuchun's Guli auxiliaries and sent their squad leaders Woshan and Wotuo to summon the people, then dispatched the tribal chief Xiebo to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lapei fell, Shizu took all one hundred seventeen of Wuchun's Guli auxiliaries, sent squad leaders Woshan and Wotuo to rally the people, and then dispatched Xiebo, tribal chief, to settle them.

sentences.zh: 斜缽不能訓齊其人，蒲察部故石、跋石等誘三百餘人入城，盡陷之。

translations.literal: Xiebo could not keep the people in order; Gushi and Bashi of the Pucha tribe and others lured more than three hundred into the city and destroyed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiebo could not hold them in discipline. Gushi and Bashi of the Pucha clan lured more than three hundred into the town and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 世祖治鷹道還，斜列來告，世祖使歡都為都統，破烏春、窩謀罕於斜堆，故石、跋石皆就擒。

translations.literal: When Shizu returned from repairing the hawk road, Xielie came to report; Shizu made Huandu commander-in-chief and defeated Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui; Gushi and Bashi were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was returning from the hawk road when Xielie brought word. He made Huandu commander-in-chief, broke Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui, and took Gushi and Bashi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 世祖自將過烏紀嶺，至窩謀海村，胡論加古部勝昆勃堇居，烏延部富者郭赧請分一軍由所部伐烏春，蓋以所部與烏春近，欲以自蔽故也。

translations.literal: Shizu led the army himself over Wuji ridge to Womouhai village, where Shengkun, tribal chief of the Hulun Jiagu tribe, dwelt; Guonán, a wealthy man of the Wuyan tribe, asked to detach a force through his own division to attack Wuchun—because his territory lay near Wuchun's and he wished to shelter himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu crossed Wuji ridge in person to Womouhai village, home of Shengkun, chief of the Hulun Jiagu clan. Guonán, a man of wealth in the Wuyan tribe, asked to lead a separate column through his lands against Wuchun, since his people neighbored Wuchun's and he wished to shield himself.

sentences.zh: 乃使斜列、躍盤以支軍道其所居，世祖自將大軍與歡都合。

translations.literal: He then sent Xielie and Yuepan with a detached force by way of where Guonán dwelt, while Shizu himself led the great army to join Huandu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xielie and Yuepan with a detachment by way of Guonán's country, while he marched the main host to join Huandu.

sentences.zh: 至阿不塞水，嶺東諸部皆會，石土門亦以所部兵來。

translations.literal: Reaching the Abusai River, all tribes east of the ridge assembled, and Shitu Men also came with the forces of his division.
translations.idiomatic: At the Abusai River every tribe east of the ridge gathered, and Shitu Men came with his warriors as well.

sentences.zh: 是時，烏春前死，窩謀罕聞知世祖來伐，訴於遼人，乞與和解。

translations.literal: By this time Wuchun had died earlier; hearing that Shizu was coming to attack, Womouhan appealed to the Liao people and begged for reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun was already dead. Hearing that Shizu was marching against him, Womouhan appealed to the Liao court and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 使者已至其家，世祖軍至，窩謀罕請緩師，盡以前所納亡人歸之。

translations.literal: Envoys had already reached his house when Shizu's army arrived; Womouhan asked that the troops be slowed and offered to return all fugitives previously taken in.
translations.idiomatic: Liao envoys had already reached his home when Shizu's host arrived. Womouhan asked for a halt and promised to return every fugitive he had harbored.

sentences.zh: 世祖使烏林荅故德黑勃堇往受所遣亡者。

translations.literal: Shizu sent Gudehei, tribal chief of the Ulin'a clan, to receive the fugitives he sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu sent Gudehei, tribal chief of the Ulin'a clan, to receive the returned fugitives.

sentences.zh: 窩謀罕以三百騎乘懈來攻，世祖敗之。

translations.literal: Womouhan took three hundred horsemen and, exploiting slack vigilance, attacked; Shizu defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Womouhan struck with three hundred horsemen while their guard was down; Shizu routed him.

sentences.zh: 遼使惡其無信，不復為主和，乃進軍圍之。

translations.literal: The Liao envoy despised his faithlessness and would no longer mediate peace; Shizu advanced and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao envoy, disgusted by his treachery, would mediate no further. Shizu pressed on and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 太祖衣短甲行圍，號令諸軍，窩謀罕使太峪潛出城攻之。

translations.literal: Taizu wore short armor and went about the siege line giving orders to the armies; Womouhan sent Taiyu to steal out of the city and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, in light armor, rode the siege circuit shouting orders. Womouhan sent Taiyu out by stealth to strike at him.

sentences.zh: 太峪馳馬援槍，將及太祖，活臘胡擊斷其槍，太祖乃得免。

translations.literal: Taiyu spurred his horse, levelled his spear, and was about to reach Taizu when Huolahu struck and broke the spear; only then did Taizu escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyu galloped up, spear couched, almost upon Taizu when Huolahu struck and shattered the shaft; only so did Taizu escape.

sentences.zh: 斜列至斜寸水，用郭赧計，取先在烏春軍者二十二人。

translations.literal: Xielie reached Xiecun River and, using Guonán's plan, took twenty-two men who had earlier been in Wuchun's army.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie came to Xiecun River and, following Guonán's scheme, secured twenty-two men once in Wuchun's service.

sentences.zh: 烏春軍覺之，殺二人，餘二十人皆得之，益以土軍來助。

translations.literal: Wuchun's soldiers perceived it and killed two; the remaining twenty were all taken and local troops were added to help.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun's men discovered the plot and killed two; the other twenty were taken, and local warriors joined the cause.

sentences.zh: 窩謀罕自知不敵，乃遁去。

translations.literal: Womouhan knew himself no match and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not stand, Womouhan fled.

sentences.zh: 遂克其城，盡以貲產分賚軍中，以功為次，諸部皆安輯焉。

translations.literal: The city was then taken; all goods and property were distributed among the army by order of merit, and every tribe was settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The town fell. Goods and property were divided among the troops by merit, and the tribes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 穆宗常嘉郭赧功，後以斜列之女守甯妻其子胡裏罕。

translations.literal: Muzong often praised Guonán's merit; later he gave Xielie's daughter Shouning in marriage to Guonán's son Hulihan.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong often spoke of Guonán's service; later he married Guonán's son Hulihan to Xielie's daughter Shouning.

sentences.zh: 溫敦蒲刺

translations.literal: Wendun Puci
translations.idiomatic: Wendun Puci

translations.literal: (Supplementary)
translations.idiomatic: (Supplementary)

sentences.zh: 烏春之後為溫敦氏，裔孫曰蒲刺。

translations.literal: Wuchun's descendants took the surname Wendun; a descendant was named Puci.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun's line became the Wendun clan; a descendant was named Puci.

sentences.zh: 溫敦蒲刺始居長白山阿不辛河，徙隆州移裏閔河。

translations.literal: Wendun Puci first dwelt on the Abuxin River of Changbai Mountain, then moved to Yilimin River in Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wendun Puci first lived on the Abuxin River of the Long White Mountains, then removed to the Yilimin River in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蒲刺初從希尹征伐，攝猛安謀克事，遇賊突出，力擊敗之，手殺二十餘人，用是擢修武校尉。

translations.literal: Puci early followed Xiyin on campaign, acting as deputy for the meng'an-moke office; when bandits burst forth he struck hard and defeated them, killing more than twenty with his own hand, and was thereby promoted to Xiuzhou Captain.
translations.idiomatic: Puci first campaigned under Xiyin as acting deputy in the meng'an-moke office. When bandits broke out he charged, killed twenty men with his own hand, and was raised to Xiuzhou Captain.

sentences.zh: 天德初，充護衛，遷宿直將軍，與眾護衛射遠，皆莫能及，海陵以玉鞍、銜賞之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he served as a guardsman, was promoted to Palace Guard General, and in long-distance archery among the guards none could match him; Hailing rewarded him with a jade saddle and bit.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tiande era he entered the guards, rose to Palace Guard General, and none among the guards could match him at long shots. Hailing rewarded him with a jade saddle and bit.

sentences.zh: 往曷懶路選可充護衛者，使還稱旨，遷耶盧椀群牧使，改遼州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent to the Helan circuit to select men fit to serve as guards, he returned with the emperor's approval, was made Yeluwan herd commissioner, and then made prefect of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Helan to choose men for the guards, he returned with imperial praise, was made Yeluwan herd commissioner, and then prefect of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 正隆伐宋，召為武翼軍副都總管，將兵二千，至汝州南，遇宋兵二萬餘，邀擊敗之，手殺將士十餘人。

translations.literal: During the Zhenglong campaign against Song he was summoned as deputy commander-in-chief of the Wuyi Army, leading two thousand troops; south of Ruzhou he met more than twenty thousand Song troops, intercepted and defeated them, and killed more than ten officers and soldiers with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenglong war on Song he was made deputy commander-in-chief of the Wuyi Army with two thousand men. South of Ruzhou he met twenty thousand Song troops, cut them off, routed them, and killed more than ten enemy soldiers himself.

sentences.zh: 是時，嵩、汝兩州百姓多逃去，蒲刺招集，使之複其業。

translations.literal: At this time the people of Song and Ru prefectures had largely fled; Puci gathered them and restored them to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Many had fled from Song and Ru prefectures; Puci gathered them back to their fields and trades.

sentences.zh: 改莫州刺史，征為太子左衛率府率，再遷隴州防禦使，曆鎮西、胡裏改、顯德軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Mozhou, summoned as commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard Commandery, then twice transferred to defender of Long Prefecture, and served in turn as military commissioner of Zhenxi, Huligai, and Xiande armies.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Mo, was recalled as commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard, then defender of Long, and in turn military commissioner of the Zhenxi, Huligai, and Xiande circuits.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 臘醅 弟麻產

translations.literal: Lapei; his younger brother Machan
translations.idiomatic: Lapei and his younger brother Machan

sentences.zh: 臘醅、麻產兄弟者，活刺渾水訶鄰鄉紇石烈部人。

translations.literal: The brothers Lapei and Machan were of the Heshilie tribe of He'lin township on Huocihun River.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei and Machan were brothers of the Heshilie clan in He'lin township on the Huocihun River.

sentences.zh: 兄弟七人，素有名聲，人推服之。

translations.literal: Seven brothers—they had long borne a famous name, and men yielded to them.
translations.idiomatic: Seven brothers—they were famed long before, and men deferred to them.

sentences.zh: 及烏春、窩謀罕等為難，故臘醅兄弟乘此際結陶溫水之民，浸不可制。

translations.literal: When Wuchun, Womouhan, and others made trouble, the Lapei brothers seized the moment to rally the people of the Taowen River and gradually grew beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchun and Womouhan stirred rebellion, the Lapei brothers used the moment to bind the Taowen River folk to themselves until none could check them.

sentences.zh: 其同裏中有避之者，徙於苾罕村野居女直中，臘醅怒，將攻之，乃約烏古論部騷臘勃堇、富者撻懶、胡什滿勃堇、海羅勃堇、斡茁火勃堇。

translations.literal: Some of their fellow villagers who avoided them moved among the Jurchens dwelling in the wild at Bihan village; Lapei was angered and meant to attack them, and so arranged with Saolai, tribal chief of the Wugulun tribe, the wealthy Tadan, Hushiman tribal chief, Hailuo tribal chief, and Wozhuohuo tribal chief.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers who fled them settled among wild Jurchen at Bihan village. Lapei meant to attack and called in Saolai, chief of the Wugulun tribe, the wealthy Tadan, and the chiefs Hushiman, Hailuo, and Wozhuohuo.

sentences.zh: 海羅、斡茁火間使人告野居女直，野居女直有備，臘醅等敗歸。

translations.literal: Hailuo and Wozhuohuo secretly sent word to the wild-dwelling Jurchens; they were prepared, and Lapei and the rest returned defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Hailuo and Wozhuohuo secretly warned the wild Jurchen, who stood ready; Lapei's force was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 臘醅乃由南路複襲野居女直，勝之，俘略甚眾。

translations.literal: Lapei then by the southern route struck the wild-dwelling Jurchens again, defeated them, and took many captives in plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei struck again by the southern road, routed them, and carried off a great body of captives.

sentences.zh: 海羅、斡茁火、胡什滿畏臘醅，求援于世祖。

translations.literal: Hailuo, Wozhuohuo, and Hushiman feared Lapei and sought aid from Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Hailuo, Wozhuohuo, and Hushiman, fearing Lapei, appealed to Shizu for help.

sentences.zh: 斜列以輕兵邀擊臘醅等於屯睦吐村，敗之，盡得所俘。

translations.literal: Xielie with light troops intercepted Lapei and the rest at Tunmutu village, defeated them, and recovered all the captives.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie with light troops ambushed Lapei at Tunmutu village, broke them, and recovered every captive.

sentences.zh: 臘醅、麻產驅掠來流水牧馬。

translations.literal: Lapei and Machan drove off herds and plundered along the Lailiu River.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei and Machan raided along the Lailiu, driving off horse herds.

sentences.zh: 世祖至混同江，與穆宗分軍。

translations.literal: Shizu reached the Hun Tong River and divided the army with Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu came to the Hun Tong and split forces with Muzong.

sentences.zh: 世祖自妒骨魯津倍道兼行，馬多乏，皆留之路傍，從五六十騎，遇臘醅于野鵲水。

translations.literal: Shizu himself pressed double marches from Dugulu Ford; many horses failed and were left by the roadside; with fifty or sixty riders he met Lapei at Yaque River.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu force-marched from Dugulu Ford; horses gave out and were left along the road. With fifty or sixty riders he met Lapei at Yaque River.

sentences.zh: 日已曛，臘醅兵眾，世祖兵少，歡都鏖戰，出入數四，馬中創，死者十數。

translations.literal: The sun had set; Lapei's troops were many, Shizu's few; Huandu fought fiercely back and forth several times, his horse wounded, more than ten dead.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk had fallen. Lapei's host far outnumbered Shizu's. Huandu fought back and forth through the press again and again; his horse was wounded and more than ten men fell.

sentences.zh: 世祖突陣力戰，中四創，不能軍。

translations.literal: Shizu charged the formation and fought with all his strength, received four wounds, and could not keep the army in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu broke into the enemy line and fought at the forefront until he took four wounds and could no longer command.

sentences.zh: 穆宗自庵吐渾津度江，遇敵于蒲盧買水。

translations.literal: Muzong crossed the river from Antuhun Ford and met the enemy at Pulubai River.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong crossed from Antuhun Ford and met the enemy at Pulubai River.

sentences.zh: 敵問為誰，應之曰：「歡都。」

translations.literal: The enemy asked who they were; the answer came: "Huandu."
translations.idiomatic: They called out to know who faced them. The answer came: "Huandu."

sentences.zh: 問者射穆宗，矢著於弓箙。

translations.literal: The questioner shot at Muzong; the arrow struck his bow case.
translations.idiomatic: The archer loosed at Muzong; the shaft struck his bow case.

sentences.zh: 是歲，臘醅、麻產使其徒舊賊禿罕及馳朵剽取戶魯不濼牧馬四百，及富者粘罕之馬合七百餘匹，過青嶺東，與烏春、窩謀罕交結。

translations.literal: That year Lapei and Machan sent their followers, the old outlaw Tuohan and Chiduo, to seize four hundred horses from the Hulubu pasture and more than seven hundred in all together with the wealthy Nianhan's horses; they passed east of Qingling and joined with Wuchun and Womouhan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lapei and Machan sent the outlaw Tuohan and Chiduo to rustle four hundred horses from the Hulubu pasture, seven hundred head altogether with the wealthy Nianhan's herds. They crossed east of Qingling and allied with Wuchun and Womouhan.

sentences.zh: 世祖自將伐之，臘醅等偽降，還軍。

translations.literal: Shizu led the army in person against them; Lapei and the rest feigned submission and Shizu withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu marched in person against them; Lapei and his brothers feigned surrender, and Shizu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 臘醅複求助於烏春、窩謀罕。

translations.literal: Lapei again sought aid from Wuchun and Womouhan.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei again begged Wuchun and Womouhan for aid.

sentences.zh: 窩謀罕以姑裏甸兵百有十七人助之。

translations.literal: Womouhan aided them with one hundred seventeen soldiers from Guli district.
translations.idiomatic: Womouhan sent one hundred seventeen men from Guli district.

sentences.zh: 臘醅據暮棱水，保固險阻，石顯子婆諸刊亦往從之。

translations.literal: Lapei held the Muleng River, securing himself in dangerous terrain; Pojukan, son of Shi Xian, also went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei held the Muleng River in rough country; Pojukan, son of Shi Xian, joined him as well.

sentences.zh: 世祖率兵圍之，克其軍，麻產遁去，遂擒臘醅及婆諸刊，皆獻之遼。

translations.literal: Shizu led troops to besiege them, overthrew their army, Machan fled, and Lapei and Pojukan were captured and presented to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu besieged him, broke his host, Machan fled, and Lapei and Pojukan were taken and sent to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 盡獲其兵，使其卒長斡善、斡脫招撫其眾，使斜缽撫定之。

translations.literal: All his troops were taken; squad leaders Woshan and Wotuo were sent to pacify the people, and Xiebo was sent to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: His fighters were taken whole. Squad leaders Woshan and Wotuo pacified the people, and Xiebo settled them.

sentences.zh: 複使阿離合懣察暮棱水人情，並募兵與斜缽合，語在《烏春傳》。

translations.literal: Again Alianhe Meng was sent to observe the temper of the Muleng River region and to levy troops to join Xiebo—the account is in the Wuchun biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu again sent Alianhe Meng to sound the Muleng country, raise troops, and join Xiebo—the full account is in the Wuchun biography.

sentences.zh: 世祖既沒，肅宗襲節度使。

translations.literal: After Shizu's death Suzong inherited the military commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu died Suzong succeeded to the military commissionership.

sentences.zh: 麻產據直屋鎧水，繕完營堡，招納亡命，杜絕往來者。

translations.literal: Machan held Zhiwu on the Kai River, repaired and completed stockades, gathered fugitives, and cut off travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Machan held Zhiwu on the Kai River, rebuilt his forts, gathered fugitives, and cut the roads.

sentences.zh: 恃陶溫水民為之助，招之不聽，使康宗伐之。

translations.literal: Relying on the people of the Taowen River to aid him, he would not heed summons; Suzong sent Kangzong to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He relied on the Taowen River folk and would not answer summons; Suzong sent Kangzong against him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，白山混同江大溢，水與岸齊，康宗自阿鄰岡乘舟至於帥水，舍舟沿帥水而進。

translations.literal: That year the Hun Tong on the White Mountains flooded greatly; water rose level with the banks; Kangzong from A'lingang took boats to the Shuai River, left the boats and advanced along the Shuai River.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Hun Tong flooded at the White Mountains until water met the banks. Kangzong took boats from A'lingang to the Shuai River, then left the boats and marched along its bank.

sentences.zh: 使太祖從東路取麻產家屬，盡獲之。

translations.literal: Taizu was sent by the eastern route to seize Machan's household; all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was sent by the eastern road to take Machan's household; all were captured.

sentences.zh: 康宗圍麻產急，太祖來會軍，於是麻產先亡在外，其人乘夜突圍遁去。

translations.literal: Kangzong pressed the siege of Machan hard; Taizu came to join the army; Machan himself was already abroad, but his men broke out by night and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong pressed the siege hard. Taizu joined the host. Machan himself was abroad, but his men broke out under cover of night and fled.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「麻產之家蕩盡矣，走將安歸。」

translations.literal: Taizu said: "Machan's household is utterly gone; where can flight lead him?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said: "Machan's house is stripped bare. Where can he run?"

sentences.zh: 追之。

translations.literal: He pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu gave chase.

sentences.zh: 麻產不知太祖急求己也，與三騎來伺軍，其一人墜馬下，太祖識之，問狀。

translations.literal: Machan did not know Taizu was urgently seeking him; with three riders he came to spy on the army; one man fell from his horse; Taizu recognized him and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Machan did not know Taizu was hunting him so hard. He came with three riders to scout the army; one fell from his horse. Taizu knew the man and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「我隨麻產來伺軍，彼走者二人，麻產在焉。」

translations.literal: The man said: "I followed Machan to spy on the army; those who fled are two men, and Machan is among them."
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "I came with Machan to watch your host. Two men fled—and Machan is one of them."

sentences.zh: 麻產與其人分道走，太祖命劾魯古追東走者，而自追西走者。

translations.literal: Machan and the man split and fled; Taizu ordered Heligu to pursue those fleeing east, while he himself pursued those fleeing west.
translations.idiomatic: Machan and his companion split up and ran. Taizu sent Heligu after the pair fleeing east and took the western trail himself.

sentences.zh: 至直屋鎧水，失麻產不見，急追之，得遺甲于路，跡而往，前至大澤，濘淖。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhiwu on the Kai River, he lost sight of Machan; pressing the pursuit, he found abandoned armor on the road, followed the trail forward to a great marsh—mire and bog.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhiwu on the Kai River he lost Machan altogether. He pressed on, found armor dropped along the road, followed the trail to a great marsh, and sank into mud and mire.

sentences.zh: 麻產棄馬入萑葦，太祖亦棄馬追及之，與之挑戰。

translations.literal: Machan abandoned his horse and entered the reeds; Taizu too abandoned his horse, overtook him, and engaged him in combat.
translations.idiomatic: Machan left his horse and plunged into the reeds. Taizu did the same, caught him on foot, and closed to fight.

sentences.zh: 烏古論壯士活臘胡乘馬來，問曰：「此何人也。」

translations.literal: Huolahu, a stalwart of the Wugulun, came on horseback and asked: "Who is this man?"
translations.idiomatic: Huolahu, a Wugulun warrior, rode up and asked, "Who is this?"

sentences.zh: 太祖初不識麻產，佯應曰：「麻產也。」

translations.literal: At first Taizu did not know Machan and answered falsely: "It is Machan."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu did not yet know Machan by sight. He answered offhand, "Machan."

sentences.zh: 活臘胡曰：「今亦追及此人邪。」

translations.literal: Huolahu said: "Have you also caught up with this man?"
translations.idiomatic: Huolahu said, "So you have run him down as well?"

sentences.zh: 遂下馬援槍進戰。

translations.literal: Then he dismounted, took up his spear, and pressed into the fight.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, levelled his spear, and joined the fight.

sentences.zh: 麻產連射活臘胡，活臘胡中二矢，不能戰。

translations.literal: Machan shot Huolahu repeatedly; Huolahu took two arrows and could not fight on.
translations.idiomatic: Machan shot again and again at Huolahu, who took two arrows and could fight no longer.

sentences.zh: 有頃，軍至，圍之。

translations.literal: Before long the army arrived and surrounded them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the main force came up and ringed them in.

sentences.zh: 歡都射中麻產首，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Huandu shot Machan in the head and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu struck Machan in the head with an arrow and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 無有識之者，活臘胡乃前扶其首而視之，見其鹵豁，曰：「真麻產也。」

translations.literal: None could recognize him; Huolahu then stepped forward, lifted his head to look, saw his prominent brow, and said: "It is truly Machan."
translations.idiomatic: No one else knew his face. Huolahu went forward, raised his head, and saw the bare ridge of his brow. "It is Machan indeed," he said."

sentences.zh: 麻產張目曰：「公等事定矣。」

translations.literal: Machan opened his eyes wide and said: "Gentlemen, your cause is settled."
translations.idiomatic: Machan fixed them with wide eyes. "Your business is done," he said."

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: Then they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Then they killed him.

sentences.zh: 太祖獻馘于遼。

translations.literal: Taizu presented the severed heads to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent the heads to the Liao court as tribute.

sentences.zh: 鈍恩，阿裏民忒石水紇石烈部人。

translations.literal: Dun'en was a man of the Heshilie tribe on the Aliminteshi River.
translations.idiomatic: Dun'en was of the Heshilie clan on the Aliminteshi River.

sentences.zh: 祖曰劾魯古，父納根涅，世為其部勃堇。

translations.literal: His grandfather was named Heligu, his father Nagenie; for generations they had been beljen of that tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Heligu and his father Nagenie; for generations their line had held the beljenate of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 斡准部人冶刺勃堇、海葛安勃堇暴其族人斡達罕勃堇及諸弟屋裏黑、屋徒門，抄略其家，及抄略阿活裏勃堇家，侵及納根涅所部。

translations.literal: Yezhi Bolie of the Wozhun tribe and Haige'an Bolie oppressed their clansman Wodahan Bolie and his younger brothers Wuliihei and Wutumen, plundering their households, and plundered the household of Ahuoli Bolie as well, encroaching on Nagenie's division.
translations.idiomatic: Yezhi Bolie and Haige'an Bolie of the Wozhun clan preyed on their kinsman Wodahan Bolie and his brothers Wuliihei and Wutumen, looting their homes. They raided Ahuoli Bolie's household too and pushed into Nagenie's territory.

sentences.zh: 穆宗使納根涅以本部兵往治冶刺等。

translations.literal: Muzong sent Nagenie with troops of his own tribe to punish Yezhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong sent Nagenie with men of his own tribe to bring Yezhi and his fellows to account.

sentences.zh: 行至蘇濱水，輒募人為兵，主者拒之，輒抄略其人。

translations.literal: Reaching the Subin River, he repeatedly pressed men into service; the local headmen refused, and he repeatedly plundered the people.
translations.idiomatic: On the Subin River he began pressing men into his ranks at every stop. When headmen refused, he plundered them instead.

sentences.zh: 遂攻烏古論部敵庫德，入米里迷石罕城。

translations.literal: He then attacked Dikude of the Wugulun tribe, entering Milimishi Han City.
translations.idiomatic: He turned on Dikude of the Wugulun and stormed Milimishi Han City.

sentences.zh: 及斡賽、冶訶來問狀，止蘇濱水西納木汗村，納根涅止蘇濱水東屋邁村。

translations.literal: When Wo Sai and Yehe came to inquire into the affair, they halted at Namuhan village west of the Subin River, while Nagenie halted at Wumai village east of the Subin River.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo Sai and Yehe came to investigate, they camped at Namuhan on the west bank of the Subin while Nagenie held Wumai on the east.

sentences.zh: 納根涅雖款伏而不肯征償，時甲戌歲十月也。

translations.literal: Nagenie though submissive in appearance refused to make restitution for what he had taken—it was the tenth month of the jiaxu year.
translations.idiomatic: Nagenie bowed and yielded in form but would not pay back what he had seized. It was the tenth month of the jiaxu year.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，納根涅遁去，斡賽追而殺之，執其母及其妻子以歸，而使鈍恩複其所。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year Nagenie fled; Wo Sai pursued and killed him, seized his mother and wife and children and returned, and had Dun'en restore his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the following year Nagenie fled. Wo Sai ran him down and killed him, brought back his mother, wife, and children, and put Dun'en back in his father's seat.

sentences.zh: 留可，統門、渾蠢水合流之地烏古論部人，忽沙渾勃堇之子。

translations.literal: Liuke was a man of the Wugulun tribe at the place where the Tongmen and Hunchun rivers meet, son of Hushahun Bolie.
translations.idiomatic: Liuke was of the Wugulun where the Tongmen and Hunchun rivers join, son of Hushahun Bolie.

sentences.zh: 詐都，渾蠢水安春之子也。

translations.literal: Zhadu was son of Anchun of the Hunchun River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhadu was son of Anchun on the Hunchun River.

sentences.zh: 間誘奧純、塢塔兩部之民作亂。

translations.literal: In secret they incited the peoples of the Aochun and Wuta tribes to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Between them they secretly stirred the Aochun and Wuta tribes to revolt.

sentences.zh: 敵庫德、鈍恩皆叛而與留可、詐都合。

translations.literal: Dikude and Dun'en both rebelled and joined with Liuke and Zhadu.
translations.idiomatic: Dikude and Dun'en broke away and threw in with Liuke and Zhadu.

sentences.zh: 兩黨揚言曰：「徒單部之黨十四部為一，烏古論部之黨十四部為一，蒲察部之黨七部為一，凡三十五部。

translations.literal: The two factions proclaimed: "The Toudan faction unites fourteen tribes as one, the Wugulun faction unites fourteen tribes as one, the Pucha faction unites seven tribes as one—in all thirty-five tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides cried abroad, "Fourteen Toudan tribes stand as one, fourteen Wugulun tribes as one, seven Pucha tribes as one—thirty-five tribes in all.

sentences.zh: 完顏部十二而已，以三十五部戰十二部，三人戰一人也，勝之必矣。」

translations.literal: The Wanyan have only twelve; with thirty-five tribes to fight twelve, three men to one—we are sure to win."
translations.idiomatic: The Wanyan have only twelve. Thirty-five against twelve means three men for every one of theirs. Victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 世祖降附諸部亦皆有離心。

translations.literal: Even among the tribes Shizu had brought to submission, disaffection was widespread.
translations.idiomatic: Even tribes Shizu had already won over began to waver.

sentences.zh: 當是時，惟烏延部斜勒勃堇及統門水溫蒂痕部阿裏保勃堇、撒葛周勃堇等皆使人來告難。

translations.literal: At that time only Xiele Bolie of the Wuyan tribe and Aribao Bolie of the Wendihen tribe on the Tongmen River, Sagezhou Bolie, and others all sent messengers reporting their distress.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Xiele Bolie of the Wuyan, Aribao Bolie of the Wendihen on the Tongmen River, Sagezhou Bolie, and a few others send envoys pleading for help.

sentences.zh: 斜勒，達紀保之子也，先使其兄保骨臘來，既而以其甲來歸。

translations.literal: Xiele was son of Dajibao; he first sent his elder brother Baogulan; afterward he came over with his armored men.
translations.idiomatic: Xiele was son of Dajibao. He first sent his elder brother Baogulan, then followed with his own armored fighters.

sentences.zh: 阿裏保等曰：「吾等必不從亂，但乞兵為援耳。」

translations.literal: Aribao and the others said: "We will certainly not join the rebellion, but we beg only troops as reinforcement."
translations.idiomatic: Aribao and his fellows said, "We will not join the rebels—we ask only for troops to hold them off."

sentences.zh: 穆宗使撒改伐留可，使謾都訶伐敵庫德。

translations.literal: Muzong sent Sagai to campaign against Liuke and Manduhe against Dikude.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong sent Sagai against Liuke and Manduhe against Dikude.

sentences.zh: 既而太祖以七十甲詣撒改軍，中道以四十甲與謾都訶。

translations.literal: Then Taizu went with seventy armored men to Sagai's army; en route he gave forty armored men to Manduhe.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then marched seventy armored men to Sagai's host and, on the way, detached forty to Manduhe.

sentences.zh: 石土門之軍與謾都訶會于米里迷石罕城下。

translations.literal: Shitu Men's army joined Manduhe below Milimishi Han City.
translations.idiomatic: Shitu Men's column joined Manduhe beneath the walls of Milimishi Han City.

sentences.zh: 而鈍恩將援留可，聞謾都訶之兵寡，以為無備，而未知石土門之來會也，欲先攻謾都訶。

translations.literal: Dun'en was about to reinforce Liuke; hearing Manduhe's troops were few, he thought them undefended and, not knowing Shitu Men had come to join him, wished to attack Manduhe first.
translations.idiomatic: Dun'en was marching to relieve Liuke. Hearing Manduhe had only a thin force, he judged the camp undefended—he did not know Shitu Men was coming—and meant to strike Manduhe first.

sentences.zh: 謾都訶、石土門迎擊，大破鈍恩。

translations.literal: Manduhe and Shitu Men met them in attack and routed Dun'en utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Manduhe and Shitu Men met him head-on and shattered Dun'en's host.

sentences.zh: 米里迷石罕城遂降，獲鈍恩、敵庫德，皆釋弗誅。

translations.literal: Milimishi Han City thereupon surrendered; Dun'en and Dikude were captured and both were released without execution.
translations.idiomatic: Milimishi Han City surrendered. Dun'en and Dikude were taken but spared.

sentences.zh: 太祖至撒改軍，明日遂攻破留可城，城中渠帥皆誅之，取其孥累貲產而還。

translations.literal: Taizu reached Sagai's army; the next day they stormed and took Liuke's city; the chieftains in the city were all executed; their wives, children, goods, and wealth were taken and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu joined Sagai. The next day they stormed Liuke's city, executed every chief within the walls, and marched home with wives, children, and goods.

sentences.zh: 塢塔城亦撒守備而降。

translations.literal: Wuta City too withdrew its garrison and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wuta City too pulled back its garrison and submitted.

sentences.zh: 留可先在遼，塢塔已脫身在外，由是皆未獲。

translations.literal: Liuke was already in Liao, and Wuta had slipped away abroad—thus neither was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Liuke was already in Liao and Wuta had slipped the net abroad, so neither was caught.

sentences.zh: 詐都亦詣蒲家奴降，太祖釋之。

translations.literal: Zhadu also went to Pu Jianu to submit; Taizu released him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhadu surrendered to Pu Jianu as well, and Taizu let him go.

sentences.zh: 於是，諸部皆安業如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon all tribes resumed their occupations as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every tribe returned to its old ways in peace.

sentences.zh: 久之，留可、塢塔皆來降。

translations.literal: After a long while Liuke and Wuta both came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In time Liuke and Wuta both came in and submitted.

sentences.zh: 阿疏，星顯水紇石烈部人。

translations.literal: A Shu was a man of the Heshilie tribe on the Xingxian River.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu was of the Heshilie clan on the Xingxian River.

sentences.zh: 父阿海勃堇事景祖、世祖。

translations.literal: His father Ahai Bolie had served Jingzu and Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ahai Bolie had served Jingzu and Shizu.

sentences.zh: 世祖破烏春還，阿海率官屬士民迎謁於雙宜大濼，獻黃金五鬥。

translations.literal: When Shizu returned victorious over Wuchun, Ahai led officials and people to welcome him at Shuangyi Great Marsh and presented five pecks of gold.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu returned from defeating Wuchun, Ahai led officials and commoners to greet him at Shuangyi Great Marsh with five pecks of gold.

sentences.zh: 世祖喻之曰：「烏春本微賤，吾父撫育之，使為部長，而忘大恩，乃結怨於我，遂成大亂，自取滅亡。

translations.literal: Shizu instructed them, saying: "Wuchun was originally of low station; my father nurtured him and made him a tribal chief, yet forgetting great favor he bore resentment against us, and thus arose great rebellion—he brought ruin on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu addressed them: "Wuchun was born low. My father raised him up and made him a tribal chief. He forgot that debt, turned against us, and brought on this great rebellion—he destroyed himself.

sentences.zh: 吾與汝等三十部人之人，自今可以保安休息。

translations.literal: I and you people of the thirty tribes—from today you may keep safe and rest in peace.
translations.idiomatic: You people of the thirty tribes and I—from this day you may live in safety and peace.

sentences.zh: 吾大數亦將終。

translations.literal: My allotted span too is nearing its end.
translations.idiomatic: My own span of years is nearly spent as well.

sentences.zh: 我死，汝等當念我，竭力以輔我子弟，若亂心一生，則滅亡如烏春矣。」

translations.literal: When I die you must remember me and strive with all your strength to assist my sons and younger kin; if a rebellious heart is once born, ruin will come as it did to Wuchun."
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, remember me and give my sons and kin your full strength. Let a rebellious heart stir once, and you will perish as Wuchun did."

sentences.zh: 阿海與眾跪而泣曰：「太師若有不諱，眾人賴誰以生，勿為此言。」

translations.literal: Ahai and the multitude knelt and wept, saying: "If the Grand Preceptor should suffer misfortune, on whom would the multitude rely to live? Speak not such words."
translations.idiomatic: Ahai and the crowd knelt and wept. "If misfortune should befall the Grand Preceptor, whom shall we live by? Do not speak so."

sentences.zh: 未幾，世祖沒，阿海亦死，阿疏繼之。

translations.literal: Before long Shizu died; Ahai also died; A Shu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shizu died, then Ahai; A Shu succeeded his father.

sentences.zh: 阿疏自其父時常以事來，昭肅皇后甚憐愛之，每至，必留月餘乃遣歸。

translations.literal: From his father's time A Shu had often come on business; Empress Zhaosu cherished him greatly—whenever he came she kept him more than a month before sending him home.
translations.idiomatic: From his father's day A Shu had often come on tribal business. Empress Zhaosu doted on him; whenever he arrived she kept him more than a month before letting him go home.

sentences.zh: 阿疏既為勃堇，嘗與徒單部詐都勃堇爭長，肅宗治之，乃長阿疏。

translations.literal: After A Shu became bolie he once disputed precedence with Zhadu Bolie of the Toudan tribe; Suzong judged the matter and ruled A Shu the senior.
translations.idiomatic: Once A Shu became bolie he quarrelled with Zhadu Bolie of the Toudan over precedence. Suzong heard the case and ruled for A Shu.

sentences.zh: 穆宗嗣節度，聞阿疏有異志，乃召阿疏賜以鞍馬，深加撫諭，陰察其意趣。

translations.literal: When Muzong succeeded to the commission, hearing A Shu harbored disloyal intent, he summoned A Shu and bestowed saddle and horse, treating him with deep reassurance while secretly probing his inclinations.
