translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the military commission he heard A Shu was turning disloyal. He summoned him, gave saddle and horse, spoke him fair words, and watched his intent in secret.

sentences.zh: 阿疏歸，謀益甚，乃斥其事。

translations.literal: A Shu returned and his plotting grew worse; Muzong thereupon exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu went home and plotted all the harder. Muzong then laid the matter bare.

sentences.zh: 複召之，阿疏不來，遂與同部毛睹祿勃董等起兵。

translations.literal: He summoned him again; A Shu did not come and therefore rose in arms with Maodulu Boliedong and others of his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned him again. A Shu would not come and rose in arms with Maodulu Boliedong and others of his clan.

sentences.zh: 穆宗自馬紀嶺出兵攻之。

translations.literal: Muzong marched from Majiling to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong marched out from Majiling to attack him.

sentences.zh: 撒改自胡論嶺往略，定潺春、星顯兩路，攻下鈍恩城。

translations.literal: Sagai advanced from Hulun Ridge to overrun, settling the Chanchun and Xingxian routes, and stormed Dun'en City.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai came down from Hulun Ridge, secured the Chanchun and Xingxian roads, and took Dun'en City.

sentences.zh: 穆宗略阿茶檜水，益募軍，至阿疏城。

translations.literal: Muzong overran the Achazhen River, further levied troops, and reached A Shu's city.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong swept the Achazhen River country, raised more troops, and came to A Shu's city.

sentences.zh: 是日辰巳間，忽暴雨，晦曀，雷電下阿疏所居，既又有大光，聲如雷，墜阿疏城中。

translations.literal: That day between the chen and si hours, suddenly a violent rainstorm; darkness and gloom; lightning struck down upon where A Shu dwelt; then again a great light, thunderous as thunder, fell within A Shu's city.
translations.idiomatic: That day between chen and si hours a sudden tempest broke. Sky and air went black. Lightning struck where A Shu dwelt; then a great flare, loud as thunder, crashed into his city.

sentences.zh: 識者以謂破亡之征。

translations.literal: Men of discernment took it as a sign of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Those who read omens called it a sign of ruin.

sentences.zh: 阿疏聞穆宗來，與其弟狄故保往訴於遼。

translations.literal: A Shu heard Muzong was coming and went with his younger brother Digubao to appeal to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Muzong was on the march, A Shu fled with his brother Digubao to plead before the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 遼人來止勿攻。

translations.literal: Liao men came ordering that they not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Liao envoys came ordering that the attack cease.

sentences.zh: 穆宗不得已，留劾者勃堇守阿疏城而歸。

translations.literal: Muzong had no choice; he left Hezhe Bolie to guard A Shu City and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong had no choice. He left Hezhe Bolie to hold A Shu City and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 金初亦有兩劾者，其一撒改父，贈韓國公。

translations.literal: In the early Jin there were also two named Hezhe: one was Sagai's father, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jin there were two men named Hezhe: one was Sagai's father, later enfeoffed Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 其一守阿疏城者，後贈特進雲。

translations.literal: The other was he who guarded A Shu City; later posthumously given the title Tejin Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The other was he who held A Shu City, later granted the posthumous title Tejin Yun.

sentences.zh: 劾者以兵守阿疏城者二年矣。

translations.literal: Hezhe had already held A Shu City with troops for two years.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhe had already garrisoned A Shu City for two years.

sentences.zh: 阿疏在遼不敢歸，毛睹祿乃降。

translations.literal: A Shu was in Liao and dared not return; Maodulu then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu stayed in Liao and dared not return. Maodulu submitted.

sentences.zh: 遼使複為阿疏來。

translations.literal: Liao envoys again came on A Shu's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Liao envoys came again on A Shu's behalf.

sentences.zh: 穆宗聞之，使烏林荅石魯濟師，且戒劾者令易衣服旗幟與阿疏城中同色，使遼使不可辨。

translations.literal: Muzong heard of it and sent Wulinzha Shiluji with troops; he also charged Hezhe to change clothing and banners to the same color as in A Shu City so Liao envoys could not tell.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong heard of it and sent Wulinzha Shiluji with troops. He also told Hezhe to match clothing and banners to those in A Shu City so the Liao envoys could not tell friend from foe.

sentences.zh: 遼使至，乃使蒲察部胡魯勃堇、邈遜勃堇與俱至劾者軍，而軍中已易衣服旗幟，與阿疏城中如一，遼使果不能辨。

translations.literal: When Liao envoys arrived, he sent Hulu Bolie and Miaosun Bolie of the Pucha tribe to go with them to Hezhe's army—but the army had already changed clothing and banners to match A Shu City exactly, and the Liao envoys truly could not distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao envoys came he sent Hulu Bolie and Miaosun Bolie of the Pucha tribe to escort them to Hezhe's camp. The garrison had already changed dress and banners to match the city. The envoys could not tell one side from the other.

sentences.zh: 劾者詭曰：「吾等白相攻，幹汝何事，誰識汝之太師。」

translations.literal: Hezhe deceitfully said: "We are merely fighting among ourselves—what business is it of yours? Who knows your Grand Preceptor?"
translations.idiomatic: Hezhe lied to them: "We are only fighting among ourselves. What is that to you? Who knows your Grand Preceptor?"

sentences.zh: 乃刺殺胡魯、邈遜所乘馬，遼使驚怖走去，遂破其城。

translations.literal: Then he stabbed and killed the horses Hu Lu and Miaosun were riding; the Liao envoys fled in fright, and the city was thereupon stormed and taken.
translations.idiomatic: He stabbed the horses Hulu and Miaosun rode. The Liao envoys fled in terror, and the city was stormed and taken.

sentences.zh: 狄故保先歸，殺之。

translations.literal: Digubao had returned first; they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Digubao had come home ahead of them. They killed him.

sentences.zh: 阿疏聞穆宗以計卻遼使，破其城，殺狄故保，複訴於遼。

translations.literal: A Shu heard Muzong had used stratagem to repulse Liao envoys, stormed his city, and killed Digubao; he appealed again to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu heard that Muzong had tricked the Liao envoys, stormed his city, and killed Digubao. He appealed to Liao again.

sentences.zh: 遼使奚節度使乙烈來問狀，且使備償阿疏。

translations.literal: Liao sent Xi military commissioner Yilie to inquire into the affair and ordered that A Shu be made whole in compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Liao sent the Xi military commissioner Yilie to investigate and ordered A Shu made whole in compensation.

sentences.zh: 穆宗複使主隈、禿荅水人偽阻絕鷹路者，而使鱉故德部節度使言于遼，平鷹路非己不可。

translations.literal: Muzong again sent men of Zhuwei and Tudai to feign obstruction of the hawk road, while sending the Biegu'de-bu military commissioner to tell Liao that only he could pacify the hawk road.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong again had the Zhuwei and Tudai river peoples pretend to block the hawk road and sent the Biegu'de military commissioner to tell Liao that none but he could reopen it.

sentences.zh: 遼人不察也，信之。

translations.literal: The Liao did not investigate and believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao court did not look into it and believed him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗畋于土溫水，謂遼人曰：「吾平鷹路也。」

translations.literal: Muzong hunted on the Tuwenshui and told the Liao men: "I have pacified the hawk road."
translations.idiomatic: Muzong hunted on the Tuwenshui and told the Liao envoys, "I have cleared the hawk road."

sentences.zh: 遼人以為功，使使來賞之。

translations.literal: The Liao took it as achievement and sent envoys to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao treated it as a service and sent envoys with rewards.

sentences.zh: 穆宗盡以其物與主隈、禿荅之人而不復備償阿疏。

translations.literal: Muzong gave all those goods to the people of Zhuwei and Tudai and did not again compensate A Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong gave the whole gift to the Zhuwei and Tudai peoples and never made A Shu whole.

sentences.zh: 遼人亦不復問。

translations.literal: The Liao too did not inquire further.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao asked no more about it.

sentences.zh: 阿疏在遼無所歸，後二年，使其徒達紀至生女直界上，曷懶甸人畏穆宗，執而送之，阿疏遂終於遼。

translations.literal: A Shu had nowhere to return in Liao; two years later he sent his follower Daji to the border of the Raw Jurchen; Yilanjian people, fearing Muzong, seized and sent him; A Shu thus ended his days in Liao.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu had no home left in Liao. Two years later he sent his man Daji to the Raw Jurchen frontier. The Yilanjian folk, fearing Muzong, seized him and handed him over. A Shu died at last in Liao.

sentences.zh: 及太祖伐遼，底遼之罪告於天地，而以阿疏亡命遼人不與為言，凡與遼往復書命必及之。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Liao, laying Liao's crimes before Heaven and Earth, he cited among them that A Shu had fled to Liao and they would not hand him over—every letter exchanged with Liao invariably mentioned it.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched against Liao he laid Liao's crimes before Heaven and Earth. Among them he counted that A Shu had fled to Liao and they would not surrender him—every letter to and from Liao named the grievance.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，闍母、婁室略定天德、雲內、甯邊、東勝等州，獲阿疏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, Zhamu and Loushi overran and settled Tiande, Yunnei, Ningbian, Dongsheng, and other prefectures, and captured A Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu, Zhamu and Loushi overran Tiande, Yunnei, Ningbian, Dongsheng, and other prefectures and took A Shu.

sentences.zh: 軍士問之曰：「爾為誰？」

translations.literal: Soldiers questioned him, saying: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: A soldier asked him, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「我破遼鬼也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I am the ghost who broke Liao."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am the wraith who broke Liao."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金之興也，有自來矣。

translations.literal: In praise it is said: The rise of Jin had long been fated.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist writes: The rise of Jin was no accident.

sentences.zh: 世祖擒臘醅、婆諸刊，既獻之遼以為功，則又曰：「若不遣還，其部人疑懼，且為亂階。」

translations.literal: Shizu captured Lapei and Pojukan; having presented them to Liao as merit, he then also said: "If they are not sent back, their tribesmen will grow suspicious and fearful and it will become a source of rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu took Lapei and Pojukan and sent them to Liao as trophies of merit. Then he said, "Unless you return them, their tribesmen will grow fearful and suspicious—and rebellion will follow."

sentences.zh: 遼人不察，盡以前後所獻罪人歸之。

translations.literal: The Liao did not perceive this and returned all culprits handed over before and after.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao court never saw through the ruse and sent back every prisoner surrendered before and since.

sentences.zh: 景祖止曷魯林牙、止同幹，穆宗止遼使阿疏城，始終以鷹路誤之，而遼人不悟。

translations.literal: Jingzu detained Helu Linya and Tonggan; Muzong detained Liao envoys at A Shu City—always misleading them with the hawk road, yet the Liao never understood.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu held up Helu Linya and Tonggan; Muzong held up Liao envoys at A Shu City. Again and again they misled the court with tales of the hawk road, and the Liao never caught on.

sentences.zh: 景祖有黃馬，服乘如意，景祖沒，遼貴人爭欲得之。

translations.literal: Jingzu had a yellow horse that rode smoothly in all ways; when Jingzu died Liao nobles competed to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu owned a yellow horse that answered every rein. When Jingzu died, Liao nobles fought to claim it.

sentences.zh: 世祖弗與，曰：「難未息也，馬不可以與人。」

translations.literal: Shizu would not give it, saying: "Hardship is not yet ended; a horse cannot be given to others."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu refused. "The trouble is not over," he said. "A war horse cannot be given away."

sentences.zh: 遂割其兩耳，謂之禿耳馬，遼貴人乃弗取。

translations.literal: He then cut off both its ears, calling it the Bald-Eared Horse, and the Liao nobles thereupon did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He cut off both its ears and called it the Bald-Eared Horse. The Liao nobles let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 其前平諸部則借遼以為己重，既獻而求之則市以為己重。

translations.literal: Earlier, in pacifying the tribes they borrowed Liao to add weight to themselves; having presented captives and then asking them back, they traded on Liao to add weight again.
translations.idiomatic: When they pacified the tribes they used Liao to magnify their own standing; when they surrendered prisoners and then demanded them back, they bargained with Liao to magnify it again.

sentences.zh: 戰陣一良馬終弗與遼人，而遼人終不悟，豈興亡有數，蓋天奪其魄歟。

translations.literal: A fine horse on the battlefield they would not give the Liao in the end, yet the Liao never understood—can rise and fall be numbered? Perhaps Heaven had taken their wits.
translations.idiomatic: They would not yield a single good war horse to the Liao, and the Liao never caught on. Perhaps fortune and ruin are fated—perhaps Heaven had stolen their judgment.

sentences.zh: 奚王回離保

translations.literal: Xiwang Huilibao
translations.idiomatic: Xiwang Huilibao

sentences.zh: 奚，與契丹俱起，在元魏時號庫莫奚，曆宇文周、隋、唐，皆號兵強。

translations.literal: The Xi rose together with the Khitan; under the Northern Wei they were called the Kumo Xi; through Northern Zhou, Sui, and Tang they were all reputed strong in arms.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi arose alongside the Khitan. Under the Northern Wei they were known as the Kumo Xi; through Northern Zhou, Sui, and Tang they were famed as formidable warriors.

sentences.zh: 其後契丹破走奚，奚西保冷陘，其留者臣服於契丹，號東、西奚。

translations.literal: Later the Khitan defeated and drove off the Xi; the Xi withdrew west to guard Lengling, while those who remained submitted to the Khitan and were called the Eastern and Western Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Khitan broke the Xi and drove them west to hold Lengling. Those who stayed behind submitted to the Khitan and were known as the Eastern and Western Xi.

sentences.zh: 厥後遼太祖稱帝，諸部皆內屬矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter when the Liao founding emperor took the throne, all the tribes came within his allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liao founding emperor proclaimed himself emperor, every tribe fell under his sway.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒者，古部族之號，奚有其地，號稱鐵勒州，又書作鐵驪州。

translations.literal: Tiele was an ancient tribal designation; the Xi held that territory and called it Tiele Prefecture, also written as Tieli Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tiele was an ancient tribal name. The Xi held that country and called it Tiele Prefecture, also written Tieli Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奚有五王族，世與遼人為昏，因附姓述律氏中，事具《遼史》，今不載。

translations.literal: The Xi had five royal clans who generation after generation intermarried with the Liao and were enrolled among the Shulü clan; the full account is in the History of Liao and is not repeated here.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi had five royal clans that for generations married into the Liao house and were enrolled among the Shulü. The details appear in the History of Liao and are omitted here.

sentences.zh: 奚有十三部、二十八落、一百一帳、三百六十二族。

translations.literal: The Xi had thirteen divisions, twenty-eight settlements, one hundred and one encampments, and three hundred sixty-two clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi comprised thirteen divisions, twenty-eight settlements, one hundred and one encampments, and three hundred sixty-two clans.

sentences.zh: 甲午歲，太祖破耶律謝十，諸將連戰皆捷，奚鐵驪王回離保以所部降，未幾，遁歸於遼。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year Taizu defeated Yelü Xieshi; the generals won victory in battle after battle; Huilibao, king of the Xi Tieli, submitted with his following, but before long fled back to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year Taizu broke Yelü Xieshi. His generals won every engagement. Huilibao, king of the Xi Tieli, surrendered with his tribesmen, but soon fled back to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 及遼主使使請和，太祖曰：「歸我叛人阿疏、降人回離保、迪裏等，余事徐議之。」

translations.literal: When the Liao sovereign sent envoys to sue for peace, Taizu said: "Return my rebel A Shu, my surrendered man Huilibao, Dili, and the rest; other matters may be discussed later."
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor sent envoys to sue for peace, Taizu replied: "Return my rebel A Shu, my deserter Huilibao, Dili, and the rest. Other matters can wait."

sentences.zh: 久之，遼主至鴛鴦濼，都統杲襲之，亡走天德。

translations.literal: After a long while the Liao sovereign reached Yuanyang Marsh; the commander-in-chief Gao attacked him, and he fled in defeat to Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: In time the Liao emperor reached Yuanyang Marsh. Commander-in-chief Gao struck him, and he fled in defeat toward Tiande.

sentences.zh: 回離保與遼大臣立秦晉國王耶律捏裏於燕京。

translations.literal: Huilibao with Liao ministers enthroned Yelü Nieli as Prince of Qin and Jin at Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Huilibao and Liao ministers set up Yelü Nieli as Prince of Qin and Jin at Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 捏裏死，蕭妃權國事。

translations.literal: When Nieli died, Consort Xiao held state affairs in her hands.
translations.idiomatic: Nieli died, and Consort Xiao held the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 太祖入居庸關，蕭妃自古北口出奔。

translations.literal: Taizu entered Juyong Pass; Consort Xiao fled out through the Ancient Northern Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu entered Juyong Pass while Consort Xiao fled north through the Ancient Northern Pass.

sentences.zh: 回離保至盧龍嶺，遂留不行，會諸奚吏民於越裏部，僭稱帝，改元天複，改置官屬，籍渤海、奚、漢丁壯為軍。

translations.literal: Huilibao reached Lulong Ridge and halted there; he assembled Xi officials and commoners at Yueli, usurped the imperial title, changed the era name to Tianfu, reorganized offices, and registered men of Bohai, Xi, and Han as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Huilibao reached Lulong Ridge and stopped. He gathered Xi officials and commoners at Yueli, declared himself emperor, adopted the era name Tianfu, reconstituted his government, and enrolled Bohai, Xi, and Han men of fighting age.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔回離保曰：「聞汝脅誘吏民，僭竊位號。

translations.literal: Taizu issued an edict to Huilibao: "We hear that you have coerced and enticed officials and people and usurped imperial titles.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu addressed Huilibao: "We hear you have coerced officials and people and stolen an imperial title.

sentences.zh: 遼主越在草莽，大福不再。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign wanders in the wilds; great fortune will not come again.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor wanders in the wilderness. Great fortune will not return.

sentences.zh: 汝之先世臣服於遼，今來臣屬，與昔何異。

translations.literal: Your forebears submitted to Liao; now you come to submit to us—how is this different from before?
translations.idiomatic: Your ancestors served the Liao. Now you would serve us. How is that a change?

sentences.zh: 汝與餘睹有隙，故難其來。

translations.literal: You and Yudu have a feud, and therefore you make his coming difficult.
translations.idiomatic: You and Yudu are at odds, and that is why you resist his coming.

sentences.zh: 餘睹設有睚眥，朕豈從之。

translations.literal: If Yudu harbors a private grudge, how should We follow it?
translations.idiomatic: If Yudu nurses a private grudge, We will not indulge it.

sentences.zh: 儻能速降，盡釋汝罪，仍俾主六部族，總山前奚眾，還其官屬財產。

translations.literal: If you can submit swiftly, all your crimes will be forgiven; you will still be made to govern the six tribal divisions, command all the Xi south of the mountains, and have your offices and property restored.
translations.idiomatic: Submit at once and your crimes will be forgiven. You shall still rule the six tribal divisions, command every Xi clan south of the mountains, and recover your offices and goods.

sentences.zh: 若尚執迷，遣兵致討，必不汝赦。」

translations.literal: If you still cling to error, troops will be sent to chastise you, and you will not be spared."
translations.idiomatic: If you persist in folly, We will send armies against you, and there will be no mercy."

sentences.zh: 回離保不聽。

translations.literal: Huilibao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Huilibao would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年五月，回離保南寇燕地，敗于景、薊間，其眾奔潰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Tianfu, Huilibao raided south into the Yan region, was defeated between Jing and Ji, and his forces scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu year 7, Huilibao raided south into Yan country, was beaten between Jing and Ji, and his army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 耶律奧古哲及甥八斤、家奴白底哥等殺之。

translations.literal: Yelü Aoguzhe together with his nephew Bajin, household slave Baidige, and others killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Aoguzhe, his nephew Bajin, the household slave Baidige, and others killed him.

sentences.zh: 其妻阿古聞之，自剄而死。

translations.literal: His wife Agu, hearing of it, cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Agu, on hearing the news, took her own life.

sentences.zh: 先是，速古部人據劾山，奚路都統撻懶招之不服，往討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, men of the Sugu tribe held Heling Mountain; Tadan, commander of the Xi route, summoned them but they would not submit, and he went to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Sugu clan held Heling Mountain. Tadan, commander of the Xi route, summoned them in vain and marched to punish them.

sentences.zh: 鐵泥部眾扼險拒戰，殺之殆盡。

translations.literal: The Tieni tribe held the defiles and resisted; nearly all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Tieni held the passes and fought back; nearly all were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 至是，速古、啜裏、鐵泥三部所據十三岩皆討平之。

translations.literal: By this time the thirteen strongholds held by the three tribes Sugu, Chuoli, and Tieni were all pacified by punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: By then the thirteen strongholds held by the Sugu, Chuoli, and Tieni clans had all been brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 達魯古部節度使乙列已降複叛，奚馬和尚討達魯古並五院司等諸部，諸部皆降，遂執乙列，杖之一百，其父及其家人先被獲者皆還之。

translations.literal: Yilie, military commissioner of the Dalugu tribe, had submitted and rebelled again; the Xi monk Mashang chastised Dalugu together with the Five Courts Office and other tribes; all submitted; Yilie was seized and given a hundred blows; his father and household members previously captured were all returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yilie, commissioner of the Dalugu tribe, had submitted and rebelled again. The monk Mashang of the Xi subdued Dalugu and the Five Courts Office along with other tribes. All surrendered. Yilie was seized and flogged a hundred times; his father and kin already in custody were restored to him.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖破遼兵于達魯古城，九百奚營來降。

translations.literal: At first, when Taizu defeated Liao troops at Dalugu City, nine hundred Xi encampments came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first broke Liao forces at Dalugu City, nine hundred Xi encampments submitted.

sentences.zh: 至是，回離保死，奚人以次附屬，亦各置猛安謀克領之。

translations.literal: By this time Huilibao was dead; the Xi submitted in turn and were each placed under commandants and battalion chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Huilibao was dead, the Xi submitted one after another, each group placed under a commander or battalion chief.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：庫莫奚、契丹起於漢末，盛于隋、唐之間，俱強為鄰國，合併為群臣，曆八百餘年，相為終始。

translations.literal: In praise it is said: The Kumo Xi and Khitan arose at the end of Han, flourished between Sui and Tang, were alike strong as neighboring states, then merged as minister and subject, passing more than eight hundred years in mutual rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist writes: The Kumo Xi and Khitan rose at the end of Han and flourished through Sui and Tang as rival powers. They became lord and subject, and for more than eight hundred years their fortunes rose and fell together.

sentences.zh: 奚有五，大定間，類族著姓有遙裏氏、伯德氏、奧裏氏、梅知氏、揣氏。

translations.literal: The Xi were five; in the Dading era, clans with recorded surnames included the Yaoli, Bode, Aoli, Meizhi, and Chuai.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi numbered five branches. In the Dading era the recorded clan surnames were Yaoli, Bode, Aoli, Meizhi, and Chuai.
